evals.prompt: I want to generate a WAV greeting for my kiosk app from the text 'Welcome, please take a ticket.' using this service's API. Show me exactly how to call it and save the result to a file.
evals.expected_output: A correct single-response synthesis walkthrough using the right endpoint, port, and field names.
expectations: Uses POST /v1/audio/speech with a JSON body containing input.
Uses port 8011 (not 8010 or 8000).
Includes model in the body (even as a placeholder) since the schema requires it, while noting it does not select the model.
Shows saving raw audio/wav bytes to a .wav file (response_format=wav, the default).
Mentions the X-Session-ID response header.

evals.prompt: My app currently calls OpenAI's real text-to-speech API and requests response_format=mp3. I want to point it at this self-hosted service instead with minimal changes. What do I need to adjust?
evals.expected_output: A correct explanation that this service only supports wav/json formats, with a concrete migration fix.
expectations: States that response_format only supports wav and json for this service, not mp3/opus/aac/flac/pcm.
Recommends changing the client to request wav (or json) instead of mp3.
Notes this service is OpenAI-compatible for the fields it supports, not a full superset of OpenAI's format list.
Suggests client-side transcoding after receiving WAV if MP3 output is a hard requirement.
Uses port 8011 in any example given.

evals.prompt: I'm sending {"model": "tts-1-hd", "input": "Hello"} expecting this service to load the tts-1-hd model, but the response still sounds like whatever it was already using. Is this a bug?
evals.expected_output: A correct explanation that the model field is accepted for compatibility only and does not select the active model.
expectations: States this is not a bug: model is accepted only for OpenAI API-shape compatibility.
States the service always uses whatever model is configured in config.yaml (models.tts.name), regardless of the request's model field.
Explains that changing the active model requires a deployment-side config change, not a per-request parameter.
Recommends GET /v1/audio/voices to confirm which model is actually active.
Does not suggest retrying with a different model string as a fix.

evals.prompt: My team told me our text-to-speech deployment uses Qwen3-TTS with voice_design, but I can't get a response from GET /health at all — not even an error, just nothing. Is my client code wrong, or is this a deployment issue?
evals.expected_output: A correct diagnosis that this is a known Qwen3-TTS startup dependency failure, not a client-side problem.
expectations: States that Qwen3-TTS currently cannot start on any device (CPU, GPU, or NPU) due to a qwen-tts/transformers version conflict.
Explains this is a service-startup failure, not a per-request error, so no client-side request change will fix it.
Recommends checking the deployment's container logs for a qwen-tts not installed error to confirm.
Recommends SpeechT5 or Kokoro as the currently deployable alternatives to raise with the deployment owner.
Does not suggest the issue is a malformed request body or missing voice/instructions field.

evals.prompt: I want to stream longer narration text so playback can start before the whole thing is synthesized. How do I consume this service's streaming endpoint correctly, and what should I do if I only ever get one event back?
evals.expected_output: A correct SSE streaming client walkthrough that also explains the single-event case is normal.
expectations: Uses POST /v1/audio/speech/stream for streaming rather than the single-response endpoint.
Describes parsing data: {...} events and decoding audio_base64 per event.
States that the stream terminates with data: [DONE].
Explains that a backend without incremental decoding may emit exactly one event before [DONE], and this is expected, not a bug.
Mentions checking for an error key in an event instead of assuming every event carries audio.

evals.prompt: A streaming request for a string that's just a bunch of punctuation marks (something like '... !! ,,,') returns a stream that closes almost immediately with some kind of error payload instead of audio. Is the service broken?
evals.expected_output: A correct explanation of the no-pronounceable-characters edge case as expected behavior.
expectations: States this is expected behavior, not a bug or dropped connection.
Identifies the cause as the input having no pronounceable characters after text normalization.
Describes the event shape as {"error": "Input text contains no pronounceable characters"} followed by [DONE].
Recommends validating/sanitizing input client-side before sending it if this case should be avoided.
Does not suggest retrying the same request will produce a different result.

evals.prompt: I don't know whether the currently running deployment is SpeechT5 or Qwen, and I want to pass speaking-style instructions like 'speak cheerfully'. How do I find out whether that will even work before I try it?
evals.expected_output: A correct recommendation to check the active model first, with accurate per-model instructions support.
expectations: Recommends calling GET /v1/audio/voices (or checking config.yaml) to determine the active model before composing the request.
States that SpeechT5 rejects instructions outright with HTTP 400.
States that Qwen custom_voice accepts instructions optionally.
States that Qwen voice_design requires instructions.
Does not claim instructions always works regardless of the deployed model.

evals.prompt: I requested voice: 'Morgan' against a SpeechT5 deployment and got a 400 error instead of it just using the default voice. Shouldn't unknown voices fall back automatically?
evals.expected_output: A correct explanation that unknown voice names are rejected, not silently defaulted, plus the correct way to discover valid names.
expectations: States that an unknown voice name returns HTTP 400 rather than silently falling back to the default speaker.
Lists or references the seven bundled SpeechT5 voices (Ryan, Miles, Aaron, Nora, Elena, Kabir, Angus) or points to GET /v1/audio/voices for the authoritative list.
Mentions the CMU Arctic id aliases (e.g. bdl, jmk) are also accepted for SpeechT5.
Recommends omitting voice entirely if the default speaker is acceptable.
Does not claim this fallback behavior is a bug to be fixed client-side with retries.

evals.prompt: I set "device": "NPU" in my request to POST /v1/audio/speech, expecting it to just fall back to CPU if NPU isn't available, but I got an error instead. Shouldn't it gracefully degrade?
evals.expected_output: A correct explanation that unsupported/unavailable device selections are rejected outright by design, not silently downgraded.
expectations: States the service validates the requested device against the configured runtime/model and the devices visible inside the container, and rejects unsupported or unavailable selections.
States this is deliberate — it never silently falls back to CPU.
Notes NPU specifically is accepted as a value but is not currently functional for any model in this service.
Recommends omitting the device field to use the deployment's configured default instead.
Does not claim this is a bug to report.

evals.prompt: I called GET /v1/audio/voices expecting fields named speakers and languages like some other services in this family use, but the response has different field names. What should I actually look for?
evals.expected_output: A correct description of this service's actual GET /v1/audio/voices response field names.
expectations: States the response includes default_speaker, supported_speakers, and default_language fields.
Notes default_language is a single string, not a list.
Notes supported_speakers is a list.
Does not claim the response uses speakers or languages as field names.
Uses port 8011 in any example given.
